analysis:
Examined the three changed files.

1) ServingReadiness.swift (new, lines 10-173) is a read-only diagnostics verdict computed from the local daemon state file. It grants no authorization and does not touch routing, keys or attestation. Authorization stays coordinator-owned (TB-011, T-052/T-053). The only notable behavior is that a coordinator-sent trust.status of 'untrusted' or 'offline' maps to blocked (line 49). A missing authorization object with trustLevel 'hardware' is reported as 'authorized (legacy verification)' (line 58). This is display-only, so it is a UX or misreporting concern rather than a control (T-052 and T-058 overclaim risk is limited, since the file's own header says diagnostics only). The 'fix' strings embed BuildEnvironment.current.coordinatorHTTPURL into a `curl | bash` reinstall hint (line 145). That URL is build-controlled, not attacker-supplied, but it is a user-facing install suggestion that should stay tied to the official build environment. Coordinator-provided `reason` strings are interpolated into advice text (lines 109, 118, 121). The text is shown locally as a CLI diagnostic, with no execution or log-public path visible.

2) ProviderLogger.swift adds three fixed enum cases (lines 147-149) to the closed public-log vocabulary. They carry no associated values, no request-derived text, and only the {cli} substitution. This preserves the public/private logging contract.

3) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift adds a call to superviseServingAuthorization() (line 82) in capacityRefreshTick. The implementation is not in the supplied evidence. The log message 'not authorized for at least 15 min; re-registering it' implies the function can force a re-registration or reconnect. Questions for the next pass: whether it is rate-limited, whether it could cause a reconnect loop or availability impact (T-057), whether it interacts correctly with endpoint-resumption and nonce handling (T-053), and whether any logged state leaks identifiers. No concrete vulnerability can be asserted from the visible diff.
